chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Abu Ibrahim al-A'jamy, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The believer is forbearing; he does not act foolishly, and if foolishness is shown to him, he forbears. He does not oppress, and if he is oppressed, he forgives. He is not stingy, and if stinginess is shown to him, he is patient.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical characteristics of a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the ethical resilience of the believer, emphasizing that true faith manifests as active forbearance rather than passive weakness. It reflects the Shia concept of *hilm* as a deliberate spiritual discipline where the believer absorbs injustice with grace, mirroring the divine attribute of *Al-Halim*. The triad of responding to ignorance, oppression, and stinginess with patience and forgiveness underscores the believer's internal stability independent of external treatment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Abu Ibrahim Al A’jamy, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momin is forbearing. Neither does he ignore (anyone), and if he is ignored upon, he forbears, nor does he oppress (anyone), and if he is oppressed, he forgives, nor is he stingy, and if he is been stingy upon, he is patient’.
en.sarwar: 17. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Uramah from (abu) Ibrahim al-‘A’jami from certain individuals of our people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

A believer is forbearing. He is not ignorant and if he is ignored he remains forbearing. He does not do injustice and if he is oppressed he forgives. He is not stingy, if stinginess is exercised against him he exercises patience.”
